source_snapshot.items: Bad Page Threshold Exceed: Default RMA Threshold
source_snapshot.procedure: Reset RAS EEPROM on devices 0..7, perform an approved warm restart, verify an empty mapped bad-page baseline, inject d0/b2/t8 iteratively on device 0 until the count first exceeds the default 128 threshold (example 144), collect Dump/EventLog/in-band CPER and then restore state.
source_snapshot.criteria: Injection may report Bus error; BMC must report HBM bad-page-count-limit exceeded for the correct OAM, with fatal threshold CPER and related reset evidence.
source_snapshot.script: No Script; 60/60 minutes; code duplicated by unrelated row 1531 thermal variant.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; suggests a parameter but omits the all-device persistent reset, bounded repeated poison, 128/144 oracle, multi-log/reset evidence and duplicate identity.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION/CRITICAL; held Pending for threshold, reset scope, injection stop rule, complete evidence and recovery.

old_problem: The case combined an all-GPU persistent EEPROM clear, restart, repeated poison and selective CPER retrieval; the historical record treated threshold/readback and phase approvals as a new engineering decision and also extended a suggested RMA action into mandatory physical replacement.
disposition_reason: The Master row supplies the acceptance threshold (128), first-crossing example (144), d0/b2/t8 stimulus and exact fatal/OOB behavior. Under ED-11/12/15/16/17/20/30, execution may be parameterized to require authoritative threshold readback equal to 128, exact device mapping, a pre-approved finite injection budget and selected warm-restart recovery. If any binding differs, execution is BLOCKED rather than guessed. The source asks to validate the RMA-threshold event and suggested action; it does not prove or require an actual OAM replacement, so physical replacement is not fabricated as PASS coverage.
decision_basis: XLSX row 2090, same-row DeepSeek, GPT V2, historical record, duplicate-code analysis and ED-01 through ED-30 were reviewed; actual next formal row Functionality 2091 / Wistron-AMD SVM-00135-V003 / c2bb7b2c65a0ec87 was directly read from XLSX and manifest.
Code reuse is preserved: row 1531 variant df4b7765c30cf301 is HBM thermal stress and cannot satisfy this row's bad-page/RMA-threshold coverage.

The literal project oracle is default threshold 128, with a first observed count greater than 128 and example 144; PASS is prohibited unless an authoritative live/config readback confirms 128 before mutation.
The 0..7 EEPROM clear is persistent and must be restricted to an approved eight-device map, preceded by complete bad-page/EEPROM evidence and followed by one exact approved warm restart.

Repeated d0/b2/t8 actions are planned threshold stimuli, not failure retries: authorize a finite maximum count, inspect the bad-page total after every action and stop at the first crossing or any anomaly.

Collect every new Dump/EventLog attachment plus in-band CPER; require the intended OAM's fatal UMC threshold record, critical message and correlated mode2/GPU reset/health chronology rather than selecting one file.
The CPER suggested action `RMA the Failing OAM` is evidence to verify, not proof that physical replacement occurred; actual service remains separately owned if the project requests it.
No EEPROM reset, reboot/warm reset, module load, mapping, injection, CPER/EventLog access, RMA, recovery, retry or DUT action was performed.

test_case.test_name: Bounded default-128 HBM bad-page RMA-threshold crossing
test_case.purpose: From an authorized clean persistent baseline, grow bad pages on one mapped OAM under a fixed finite budget until the verified default threshold 128 is first crossed, then prove the platform's fatal threshold alert, CPER, reset and recovery behavior.
required_package: Approved amdgpuras, amd-smi and cdump_analyzer versions plus authenticated paginated Redfish Dump/EventLog access
Authoritative project/firmware threshold readback proving 128 before execution
Immutable eight-device/card/BDF/OAM map and selected target device 0
Approved EEPROM-clear scope, one exact warm-restart method and complete recovery
Per-injection bad-page counter, maximum action budget, isolation, console/power and qualified operator
test_case.test_command: Phase A: preserve complete per-device EEPROM/bad-page/topology and OOB/in-band evidence; after approval run the reset only for the eight mapped test GPUs, then perform the one selected warm restart and prove the target baseline is empty. Phase B: after separate approval execute `sudo amdgpuras -d 0 -b 2 -t 8` one planned action at a time, recording output and the target bad-page count after each; stop immediately at the first count >128 or any anomaly and never exceed the approved budget. Phase C: collect complete protected Dump/EventLog attachments, in-band CPER and reset/health evidence before separately approved recovery. Do not clear logs or blindly repeat.
test_case.expected_result: With live threshold readback 128, counts progress deterministically from the approved clean baseline and the first crossing is recorded (144 only if that is the observed/source-consistent first count). The intended OAM produces the HBM bad-page-count-limit critical event, fatal UMC threshold CPER with ext0 Bad-page-retirement-threshold-exceed description, expected mode2/GPU reset evidence and matching in-band CPER, then reaches the signed recovery state.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires row/variant identity, verified threshold=128, approved eight-GPU reset/restart, monotonic per-action counts with a hard first-crossing stop, complete OOB/in-band fatal evidence on the correct OAM, reconciled reset behavior and healthy recovery. FAIL on threshold mismatch after start, unbounded/repeated action, wrong OAM, non-monotonic or unexplained counts, missing/selected-only evidence, unexpected device loss or failed recovery. Before mutation, any threshold/map/approval gap is BLOCKED.
safety_gate: Gate CLOSED until live default threshold 128, exact eight-GPU scope, target map, maximum injection count and recovery are signed.
Use separate point approvals for persistent EEPROM reset/restart, bounded poison phase and recovery.
Preserve all historical bad-page, CPER, EventLog and topology evidence before reset; never clear logging evidence.
Stop at first count above 128 or immediately on abnormal count, unexpected OAM/reset, instability or evidence gap; no automatic retry.
expected_evidence: Exact duplicate-code row/variant map and source hash
Signed threshold=128 readback, eight-device/OAM map, action budget and phase approvals
Per-device pre-reset EEPROM/bad-page state, reset outputs and selected restart transition to OS/GPU ready
Target empty baseline plus every injection output and monotonic after-action count through first crossing
Complete authenticated Dump/EventLog manifests, all new raw/decoded attachments and in-band CPER
Correct OAM fatal threshold/ext0 record, critical message, mode2/GPU reset correlation, suggested-action text, final recovery and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: At first crossing or anomaly, cease all injection and seal evidence. Do not reset EEPROM again or inject further. Apply only the approved recovery, preserve any service/RMA recommendation, and quarantine the OAM/node if topology, GPU health or bad-page state fails the signed exit criteria.

source_conflict.reason: The rewrite binds the literal 128 oracle to mandatory readback, replaces unbounded repetition/selective logs with a capped first-crossing procedure and preserves the duplicate variant without inventing physical replacement coverage.

blocked.reason: The test method and literal threshold oracle are defined; missing live readback, mapping, approvals or recovery are runtime project prerequisites.

pending.unlock_condition: Provide authoritative threshold=128 readback and approve every runtime phase; any differing threshold requires owner reconciliation before execution, not a new guessed value.
